speechtext:
In connection with
Housing Enterprises Limited, I understand the schedule of rentals runs $42, $47, and, I believe, about $55. Is that the average across the country wherever these houses were built?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That is the general rental range, but there are more expensive apartments.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: In the contracts made with tenants, is it true that no tenant who is, let us say, on piece work or who is doing seasonal work is acceptable in these houses?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It depends. If he is a veteran and has reasonable earnings over the year, I do not think they care whether his earnings are seasonal or not. They expect the tenant to have an income which will enable him to pay the rent that these projects demand. If he cannot pay the rent, an effort is made to get him accommodation within his means.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The minister did not grasp my meaning. Has it been necessary for a man to have an assured income over the past year, we will say, in order to be able to rent one of these houses? Suppose at the moment he is engaged on piece work or on seasonal work: on that basis, if it continued for the whole year, he would have enough to meet the requirements. Veterans tell me that they have attempted to negotiate the rental of some of these houses, more particularly at $42 or $47, and they find that simply because of the kind of employment they have there is no hope for them. Being a veteran does not help
a man at all. Can the minister enlighten the committee further as to what the practice is? Is the report made to me correct, that they cannot rent these houses for the reason I have stated?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Generally speaking the married veteran with two children is taken care of, if not with one type of house then with another, and if there is a surplus of housing beyond that, the veteran with fewer points-the married veteran with one child-is taken care of. I think the point system is more important than earnings. Of course earnings are considered. It would be foolish for a veteran to move into a class of accommodation he could not possibly pay for, and it would be foolish for the managers of the project to permit him to do so. But if he qualifies on points and has any income whatever, which all veterans have, he is taken care of.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister mentioned Housing Enterprises Limited and said they had completed some 3,000 units. Is that correct?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: How many units altogether were started by Housing Enterprises Limited?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: There were 3,313 started. They are all finished.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
In introducing the resolution on May 5 the minister, as reported at page 3640 of Hansard-there is reference to Housing Enterprises Limited-made this statement:
In light of all circumstances the government accepted this proposal. The corporation has taken over Housing Enterprises Limited and has completed and rented the 3,313 units in the 32 projects.
How many of these units did the government have to complete after they took over from Housing Enterprises Limited?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The government completed about 2,000 units. The rest were completed by the other company.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Then it would seem that Housing Enterprises completed 1,113 and the government completed 2,200. How much money had the government spent on Housing Enterprises Limited?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: When all the bills are paid- the accounts have not yet been straightened out-the cost will be about $26,000,000 for the 3,313 units.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
In reply to the hon. member for Lincoln the minister said that the rent of the units started by Housing Enter-
National Housing Act

prises Limited and completed by the government would be $40, $42 and $47. Is that correct?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It is difficult to give an overall figure, because there are so many different types of accommodation started under the plan. I should think that is a fair figure for the single units. In the city of Toronto and in one or two other cities there are apartments that rent at a much higher figure than that.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I understand that there are some apartments in Vancouver. Has the minister the rentals for those apartments? Can he give them now?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I am sorry to say we have not got them. They are substantially higher, however, than the figures named.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The reason I am inquiring particularly is that during the last session, though I have not the exact date-I believe it was on May 14-the minister referred to a firm bid that had been received for 400 units in Hamilton, and on that occasion I understood the rentals, when these units were finished, would be $55, $65 and $75. They were three-, four-, and five-room units. If the others were comparable, or if these were finished, the rentals would be away beyond what the minister has stated. I want the minister to remember I am just saying "if."

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: My impression is that when the range of rentals was placed before the government the project was not approved, and I think I am correct in saying that particular project was not actually built. When the government took over Housing Enterprises Limited it made every possible effort to reduce the rentals of the units. In some cases the amortization period was extended and interest on money was reduced, and every means was taken to bring the rentals to a reasonable level, so that today they are not too far out of line for the ordinary veteran family.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: On the basis of the figures the minister gave a few moments ago, 3,313 units at a total cost of $26,000,000 would represent $8,000 per unit. I do not see how it would be possible to rent these units at the figures mentioned by the member for Lincoln a few minutes ago. Can the minister explain how in these circumstances the rentals can be revised downwards?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
My hon. friend is correct. The average unit cost is about $8,000. The rentals were brought down by extending the amortization period and extending low interest

rates. The government owns them directly; it is not in the hands of the mortgage company today. The government has lent at the cheapest rate at which a government can lend money to a project of that sort, so that even though the units cost $8,000, the rentals are approximately as stated.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: What is the average cost of the four-room unit that Housing Enterprises Limited built?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Built in what year?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: They are just finishing them up. They were finished and then they were abandoned. There was a four-room unit that was built. What was the over-all cost of that? It looks to me as if these prices are away out of line.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We thought they were away out of line. That is why we took them over. We did not like to lend money on the houses at the amounts that they were costing.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Can we not be told what they cost?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: If the hon. member will tell me what project he is talking about, I shall be able to get the information. He waves his hand and asks, what do four-room units cost. What project is it he refers to?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Three different types of units were built in the city of St. Catharines. There were 102 houses. The four-room unit, the lesser of the three, rents for $42 per month with some other service charges added. I should like to know what that particular four-room unit cost.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We will get that.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
I have been more
specific.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We will get the information.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It seems to me we ought to have it.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: P.C. 1095 was an order in council having to do with a rental housing project in which the element of double depreciation was the main factor. It is stated in the order in council that it must be a rental housing project commenced prior to January 1, 1949. The first question I should like to ask the minister is this. If rental insurance comes in, is that the end of P.C. 1095 with respect to double depreciation?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The double depreciation was put on for a period to test its value as a

National Housing Act
stimulation to the building of apartments. The intention is to dovetail it into the rental insurance.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Will double depreciation be a factor in this rental insurance plan? Or is it a project by itself?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It was a project by itself. It was announced a year ahead of the insurance principle. The insurance principle, I am sure,-although the regulations have not yet been worked out-will only apply to ordinary depreciation. Double depreciation is a right that the owner will have, which he can take advantage of if the earnings permit; but the government would not insure sufficient earnings to guarantee his ability to take care of double depreciation.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
It seems a reasonable
conclusion that the minister does not intend that double depreciation shall be any part of this rental insurance plan.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: No.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
Coming to the rental
insurance plan, I rise to ask him some questions with respect to these items.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: May I suggest that the hon. member is now discussing details of the bill, which is not before us? Would his questions not be more appropriate when we are considering the bill?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister is quite right. As I understand it, this project of rental insurance will have nothing to do with the construction of low-cost rental houses.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It will apply to the lowest-cost apartment houses that can be built, I assure the hon. member. It is not our intention to insure rentals of luxury apartments. They must be the lowest-cost apartment buildings.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
In his remarks on the
resolution the minister referred to rentals not over $80 per month; and in his statement as reported at page 3642 of Hansard he said:
It is likely, however, that most of the new houses will be in the moderate rental field because that is the type of housing in which landlords and builders are interested.
I am suggesting to the minister that when he refers to "the moderate rental field" he means something above the low-cost field.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: No. It is the bottom of the apartment house band. Eighty dollars a month for a fully-serviced apartment-which means heat, light, and all services-is not a luxury apartment, to the best of my knowledge.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
How are the people
going to pay that?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
What does the man who
rents a house for $40 a month pay for his coal, light and other services? He pays that. The hon. member laughs.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: No, he does not pay $40 a month.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Let us be realistic about this.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: He does not pay $40 for those services.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I am not so sure.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister may not be so sure, but I know he does not. If the minister does not know that, I do.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Under this plan is it intended that not only will the builder, investor or professional landlord have sufficient revenue to take care of his taxes, interest on mortgage indebtedness, operating expenses and repairs, but over and above that, no matter what, he shall have a return of two per cent on the money which he has invested?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes. The insurance should cover those items.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: When the minister was speaking on May 5, he outlined this new principle in rental housing, this matter of rental insurance. He says that if the resolution is adopted, more detailed examination of the proposal can be made when we are in committee of the whole. As this is a new principle, I think the minister at this stage should be prepared to tell us just how it works and to give us more details than he has given today.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The bill carries the detail. We are discussing the principle today. I think the principle is fairly clear. The purpose is that for a consideration the mortgage company will issue an insurance policy which guarantees that, for a period, the revenue from the building will amount to a minimum sufficient to pay the charges which were just mentioned by the hon. member for Parkdale. That is the principle of the bill.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister mentioned a term. Do I understand that this term of guarantee for insurance will be thirty years?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
It could go up to thirty years. It will probably be for a lesser period. It will depend on the term of the mortgage agreement. Certainly it may go beyond the term of the mortgage agreement. This bill gives the right to insure for that maximum period.
National Housing Act

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The term of the mortgage is thirty years. There is a specific term in respect of the insurance. Do I understand that the government will be tied into this plan for a matter of thirty years?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Under the provisions of the bill the term of the mortgage is not to exceed twenty years. That is the difficulty which arises in discussing the bill when we have not the bill before us. As I say, if the hon. member will wait until the bill is brought down, the basic principle will be much clearer.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The resolution reads:
. . . and to make loans to owners of rental housing projects not exceeding in amount eighty-five per cent of the estimated cost thereof; to authorize central housing and mortgage corporation to guarantee an annual return of an amount to be determined by the corporation of rentals from rental housing projects for a period not exceeding thirty years . . .
Is that part and parcel of this insurance plan, and if so, what is the factor of thirty years?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It is felt that we should take power to insure the transaction to a point where the builder of the apartment can be completely paid out. It has nothing to do with the term of the mortgage, which is restricted to twenty years. The corporation, of course, will make an appropriate transaction for a special case, and it is taking the right to insure for the full term of thirty years if the circumstances seem to warrant this being done.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Then the minister said the arrangement "would retain the debtor-creditor relationship." Does this mean the builder goes on the covenant of the mortgage and remains there as an ordinary debtor in respect of the mortgage?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That is what it means.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Or does he get off it?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It means just that.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: It means which?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That he does exactly as my hon. friend says; he stays on the covenant.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: He is a convenanter?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: He has to pay for the insurance he gets?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Oh, yes.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Since we are dealing here with a principle which underlies all housing, will the minister indicate the size of the commitment his department is prepared to recommend in respect of this insurance angle? Will he also put on record the amount of money this government is obligated for in guarantees under housing up to the present time? For instance, we are obligated for a very large amount of money on loans under the National Housing Act. I understand we are also obligated to some extent in connection with Housing Enterprises Limited. We are also obligated to the builders in respect to integrated housing. Could we have something put on the record before this resolution passes which will indicate whether in fact we are not subsidizing housing now and give us some idea of the fextent to which we [DOT] are obligated?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Our cash obligation under housing act loans is about $8,000,000.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Is that the over-all?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That is on loans under the National Housing Act. That is what our cash guarantee to the mortgage companies amounts to.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We are obligated for hundreds of millions of dollars, are we not, in respect of all our housing enterprises?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Housing Enterprises has been taken over and paid out. We own it.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I was not referring specifically to that corporation, but to all our housing projects.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: My hon. friend would like to know how much money the government has invested in housing?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: No, not particularly what we have invested, but the amount of guarantees we have given.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: About $8,000,000. Those are the guarantees in the mortgage pool. We have an insurance pool on National Housing Act loans, and at the moment our liability to that pool is about $8,000,000.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Then in respect of this rental insurance, does it contemplate detached and semi-detached houses as well as multiple houses? Would a person building eight houses come under this scheme, or must it be multiple housing?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
There must be eight family units involved. It does not matter whether it

National Housing Act
is horizontal or vertical, as long as there are eight units involved in one building.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That is the minimum?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I think I am in order in referring to a question I asked the minister on May 3, which appears at page 3535 of Hansard. At that time the minister said he was going to get the information on my question, which had to do with housing in Charlottetown. As the minister knows, housing projects on behalf of veterans there have not amounted to a great deal. Some three years ago an emergency housing plan was put into operation by the city, and one hundred families of veterans are still living in this emergency accommodation at the airport. The city carried it on for one year; then the provincial government took it over and has continued it up to the present. Now they have given these one hundred families notice that they must get out within a short time, because this property has been declared surplus and will be sold1 in the course of a month or so. I wanted to know if it is the intention of the minister to continue to provide this emergency housing for these veterans until such time as his department can do some building for them.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We have no information on the proposal mentioned by my hon. friend. I might explain that the emergency shelter was provided under agreement between the city of Charlottetown and the federal government. The federal government contributed the wartime buildings and paid half the cost of conversion, and under the agreement the city was to operate the property and collect and retain the rentals. After a period the city dropped the project and refused to carry it on any further. The provincial government took over the city's obligation, so to all intents and purposes the provincial government are the owners and operators of the project. There would be no reason why they would let us know their plans, but we have not been advised of any plan such as that mentioned by my hon. friend.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
On May 5, at page 3641 of Hansard, the minister said:
The builder and the landlord know that economic rentals at today's level will see them through. However, they doubt whether present rentals will be maintained.
And at the top of the next page he went on:
This guaranteed rental will be about eighty-five per cent of the economic rental which the owner may charge his tenants during the first three years. The owner will pay a premium for his rental insurance at a rate to be set by the
5849-239i
governor in council. Provision is made for a lending institution to make loans up to eighty-five per cent of the estimated cost of the rental housing project. These are to be direct loans with all the funds to be advanced by the lending institution, rather than the usual joint loans under the National Housing Act.
The reason given was that there is very little risk involved. I submit, Mr. Chairman, that this is a very unfair type of subsidized housing. It is subsidized housing for the people who are prepared to pay up to $80 a month, and all hon. members know that this includes only a very small proportion of the Canadian people, a group who, as I mentioned the other day, somehow or other can find living quarters without subsidy. While there is no hard and fast rule, I think it has always been accepted that one should not pay more than two years' income for his housing, so the pedp'g who will occupy this housing should be those receiving at least $4,000 a year. For those getting only $1,000 a year the maximum would be $2,000. The majority of Canadians are not getting $4,000 a year and cannot afford to pay what is required to service that type of housing accommodation.
This is a case of heads I win, tails you lose, as far as the lending institutions are concerned. The minister states that under present inflated conditions landlords are prepared to build houses, and that they can find economic rentals. We are to have a three-year testing period, so it would seem that the government is counting on the depression being at least three years away. I am not one of those people who accepts the opinion that a depression is just around the corner, with the cost of living going up-

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: When did you change?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I think it is not just around the corner; it will come some time; but it is not very close.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Your story is that a depression has been around the corner since 1943.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I am not one of those who predicted a depression since 1943.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister is making provision for it in the bill.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The cost of living is going up every month, and the lending institutions are prepared to build houses now and to accept 85 per cent of the rentals during the first three years. It is obvious that they are able to get a good deal more than economic rentals at the present time. The shortage of housing is so acute that rentals run at $100, $125 or $150. as members of parliament have
National Housing Act

found when they have come to Ottawa and looked for housing accommodation during the session. One can sell or rent a house at the present time for almost any price.
The government's own publication supports my theory that we are overbuilt for people who can afford to pay for units running at $8,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Would my hon. friend tell me where he finds that quotation?

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
I have not the statistics here; but the people who can afford houses at $8,000 are those who are getting $4,000 a year or more; and your own bureau of statistics, which comes under the Department of Trade and Commerce, has published all kinds of material to support my claim that we have built more housing than can be bought and paid for by people who are getting $4,000 or $5,000 a year and upwards.
What we are doing now is to guarantee that lending institutions will have a three-year testing period, and that they will have at least 85 per cent of the maximum rentals they can collect during that period. Then, for a period of twenty or thirty years they will be guaranteed at least the taxes, the debt services, the operating expenses and a reasonable return of two per cent on the investment. I submit that this is discriminatory legislation, and that it should be carefully scrutinized by the people of Canada.
I say that if the lending institutions want a guarantee of that kind they should not be permitted to take advantage of the increase. I believe costs are likely to go up in the next year, and the lending institutions are in a position where they can take advantage of the increase in the event of prices going up. They are guaranteed 85 per cent of prevailing rates, which are well above the cost of economic rentals, over a period of time. So at this stage I offer my protest against this type of discriminatory legislation which will serve to subsidize a small group of people in the higher income brackets.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I cannot follow' my hon. friend at all. In the first place, lending institutions do not build houses. I do not know why the hon. member is talking about lending institutions; he seems to have them on the brain. I do not know of a single lending institution in Canada that builds houses, apartments or anything else. Those institutions lend the money to others who do the building. But they do not lend the full amount, and they do not collect rents.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We have not the bill before us, but it would seem that the rental insurance is limited to the class of housing which is needed the least. They will have 85 per cent of the guaranteed rentals, plus these other items I have mentioned, plus two per cent; so that they are in a perfect position. The details are not before us, but we shall have them soon. Apparently some people in Canada will have this guarantee, and it is expected that they will build some housing. If not, I do not know why we are wasting our time in a discussion of the legislation.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
It is exactly the same as the position where a life insurance company is willing to guarantee my hon. friend, by taking the risk that he will live for a certain period of time. They may be too optimistic and they may be too pessimistic, but on the average they are about right. We are not guaranteeing anything. We are selling insurance on that prospect. My hon. friend has been saying, for the last four years, that a depression is just around the comer; anybody would have been right in betting against him there; anyone who had insurance against falling rentals would have been more right than my hon. friend. If my hon. friend is right and a depression is just around the corner, it might be expensive insurance. In other words, if I am right when I say I believe that this is a growing country and that it is likely to continue to grow and prosper, it would not be expensive. In any event, the government is setting a rate which it believes protects the situation in either direction.
MR. LOCKHART: I do not wish to hold up the resolution; but I gather from what the minister has said-somewhat heatedly at times-that any information with respect to the winding up of Housing Enterprises and the taking over by Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation, and information respecting Wartime Housing Limited, will all be available when the bill is before us?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes. I had hoped to have it available now; I sent one of my officers out to get it.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Then I shall suspend until later further questions I have to ask.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
I am glad the minister is so sure there will be no depression. If we could get that optimistic assurance over to the builders who build the houses we might have some houses built. That is the trouble, as was indicated the other day when he intro-

National Housing Act
duced the resolution; he cannot get the builders to see it that way. Consequently the government or the people of Canada have to take the shock.
At page 3641 of Hansard he said:
We have made a careful examination to ascertain the main reason for lack of rental housing by the entrepreneur. A number of -builders engaged in the rental field have been interviewed and the whole situation has been thoroughly canvassed. It will be remembered that rentals upon new units are no longer under rental control.
The field has been cleared for them. He continued:
Economic rentals in relation to today's costs are readily available. It is our own belief that the main deterrent to-new rental construction is the fear that although economic rentals will support present capital costs, the day will come when comparable rental units can be built at a lesser figure, with correspondingly lesser rentals.
Well, when the depression comes, prices will fall. He continued:
The builder and the landlord know that economic rentals at today's levels will see them through. However they doubt whether present rentals will be maintained.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I might point out that we can theorize all we like. I can have my theory of the future; my hon. friend can have his, and the hon. member for Mackenzie can have his gloomy picture of the depression around the corner. But the opinion which is important is that of the investor who ordinarily builds houses, and who can build or not as he likes. Neither the hon. member nor I can pass laws or theorize in any way to compel him to build houses if he does not feel like doing so.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: The minister has just said that the investing company does not build houses.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I do not object to the minister's having theories, but I object to his finding fault with us when we have theories which agree with the theories which he finds among those who are expected to invest in houses. The fact of the matter is that investors will not invest without a government guarantee.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Probably investors believe my hon. friend. His election campaign in 1945 was fought on the belief that there was a depression just around the corner, and he had many supporters in that election. Perhaps many investors believed he was right at that time, and still believe he may be right in the future.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Apparently the minister did not follow my election campaign in 1945 very closely. He has not heard me say anything in the house about a depression. But what I do know is that under our present system a depression will come, unless the minister can find some way out. There are ways out.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I should like to ask a question based on the last part of the resolution. Provision is made for the dissolution of Wartime Housing Limited. I understand that at the present time it has under way a great many houses. Is it intended that Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation shall continue to t.ie completion of those houses, and that from *'*ear to year they shall continue with the work begun by Wartime Housing Limited? Further, is it intended that the Department of Reconstruction and Supply shall in the course of time, or shortly, go out of existence; and that housing in future will all be handled by Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation? Can the minister tell us why it was necessary to change from Wartime Housing Limited to Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
It is simply giving legal effect to a condition that exists today. Wartime Housing is a separate corporation charged with the building of houses for the federal government. The houses are owned by the crown. As a matter of fact, the staff of Wartime Housing Limited has been merged with the staff of Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation, although the two corporate identities still exist. We feel that we are getting far enough away from the war that "Wartime Housing" is no longer an appropriate name. We see no purpose in maintaining two corporate structures when one in fact is doing the work.
Wartime Housing Limited has no staff except a skeleton board of directors. Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation is collecting the rents of the houses owned by the crown in the name of Wartime Housing Limited and charging a fee for doing so. Central Mortgage is really performing the work and directing building activities.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Is it intended that Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation will conduct all housing projects in future and that the Department of Reconstruction and Supply will fold up shortly?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
I do not know that the two are related. Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation is a crown company and always has been a crown company. At the moment it reports to the Minister of Reconstruction and Supply, and it will report to some minister, regardless of the future of the Department of Reconstruction and Supply. I
National Housing Act

suppose the Department of Reconstruction and Supply will fold up when the particular functions of that department are liquidated, but I cannot say when that will be.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: What date was the rent control taken off new housing construction?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: February, 1947.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
It seems to me that there is a degree of unfairness here. I think the underlying principle for the taking off of rent control in the case of new buildings was that the cost of construction was going up and that houses were badly needed. I had an instance drawn to my attention not long ago where a house being constructed was rented at the beginning of 1947. It was a privately constructed house being built for rental purposes. This house was rented in January and the rent control was taken off in February. Although it was rented, the final completion of the house did not take place until another five or six months had passed. If I recall rightly, there were some doors between the kitchen and dining room or something like that which could not be obtained and the house was not actually completed until well after February.
Because the house was rented before the cut-off date, the rent was controlled, but another man who had completed a house just after that did not have his rent controlled. This man could have refused to rent his house on the ground that it was not fully completed. If he had waited after the cut-off date his rent would not have been controlled. I think cases like this should receive a little more consideration.
I should like to say something about the subsidizing of new houses. No doubt it would cost the government a good deal to subsidize low-rental housing. The government are taking the position that because of increased costs of construction, material and labour, they do not think it would be profitable for them to go into the housing business. They feel that they could not afford to build houses to rent at the set rentals.
Surely, if the government cannot afford to go into building, we cannot expect the private individual to enter this field. If neither the government nor the private individual goes into the construction of low-rental houses, who is to build them? There is a drastic shortage of houses, and if you take these two parties out of the building field it means that no houses will be built.
if one reviews the building permits issued by the different municipalities he will find a falling off in the building of rental houses and 
house construction generally. It is true that there is an increase in commercial building, but that will not solve the problem of rental housing. It does seem to me that the government will have to reconsider the possibility of subsidizing low-rental housing. I do not see how you are going to stimulate this type of building unless that is done. Private individuals cannot afford to erect houses at the price suggested the other day by the minister, that is, $6,800, to rent at $37.50 a month. They just cannot do it.
There is just one other thing I should like to draw to the minister's attention. I refer to the contract which has been used in the past and which I presume Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation is using. This is the standard form of contract. I spoke at some length on this a year ago when I had the contract before me and I do not propose to review at this time all that I said on that occasion.
It seems to me that when a man has made the payments required by the lending institution he should have a fair equity in his place, but the existing contract states that if a man fails even in his last payment he loses all equity in his place. In fact he could be prosecuted as a trespasser if he did not get out after having been given notice. It seems to me that that is unjust, and I think the minister should draw up a new contract where a man would have an equity in his place according to the payments he had made.
Such a provision would give some incentive to the man buying a house. He would know that, as payments were being made, his equity would be increased. Last year I placed the particular clause in the contract on Hansard. As I say, that clause would permit a man losing every cent he had paid in, and I do not think that is right. I agree that this is the standard contract, but I do not think it is a just contract. The contract should be revised and a new one made, so that the buyer will not lose all his investment. When we are discussing the clauses I shall endeavour to have the contract with me, and perhaps we can go into it then in greater detail. In the meantime I wish the minister would review the contract with a view to making it more equitable for the purchaser.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
My hon. friend spent some time in proving that no one could build a low-cost house at present prices, but in the first three months of this year there have been more houses started than in any previous three months in our history. So his reasoning is not borne out by the facts.

National Housing Act

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Is there a $7,000 house renting for $37.50?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I would not say that there is.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: That is my point. The eost is so high that the entrepreneur cannot build a house to rent at that figure.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Who knows whether next year or the year after, costs will not be higher? They were higher in 1945; they were higher in 1946; they were higher in 1947; they are higher in 1948, and possibly they will be still higher in 1949. When is a man to make up his mind whether he wants a house or not? If he is married and has a child or two he cannot just wait until prices suit him. He has to build or go without a house.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Then he may take a very great loss.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: So far as equity insurance is concerned, I do not know any way in which a man can preserve his equity other than by keeping up his payments. No one can take away a man's equity in his home except the courts, and in a case of hardship the court will appreciate the representations made.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Would not the court have to be governed in its decision partly by the contract a man signs?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Perhaps, but courts have been known to be lenient in hard cases.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
In the contract, if the
man fails to make one payment, he waives all his rights, even to go to court.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Oh, no. Nothing can take away a man's right to go to court.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Yes, according to this contract, and that is one objection I have to it.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
In connection with the winding up of Wartime Housing, I was critical of this major venture of the federal government into the housing field early in the war, on the ground that many of these would be permanent houses, but I agree readily that the people living in them were happier because they were better and more cheaply housed than they otherwise could have been. I find by the annual report of Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation, at page 55, that the estimated completed cost per unit is just over $5,000, for housing, supplementary buildings, land improvements, covering 31,000 units. At pages 44 and 45 of the report I note that these units are being sold at an average of $2,500. My understanding was that an undertaking was given to the municipalities
that the houses would not be sold but would be demolished in due course. I note, however, that in Halifax, Montreal, Quebec and Victoria these houses are being sold. I take it that the local authorities have been consulted. Would the minister make a statement as to whether or not these wartime houses are not a fairly good investment from the federal point of view, and should they be sold at $2,500' per unit when they cost $5,000, and costs have been going up since then? Most of these houses have been kept in fairly good repair and it would seem to me that it is not wise to dispose of them at this price at this time. I know the veteran deserves special consideration, but the veterans should get housing of a little better quality than wartime housing. Would not the 31,000 units be a good investment for us to keep for a few years, and does $2,500 seem a fair price to be getting for them?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The $5,000 average cost
includes a good deal of land development; in fact $13,000,000 is in there for land development. Generally speaking, the houses being sold today for $2,500 to $3,000 did not cost $5,000, although that may have been the average cost of all houses. Generally speaking, the houses now being sold were built under low-cost conditions. One reason why we are selling wartime housing is that we are in an indefinite position with regard to it. These houses were built under contract for the duration of the war and one year thereafter, and in most cases these agreements with the municipalities have not been renewed; so that we are in the position of being obliged to remove the houses from the land at any time the municipalities ask us to do so. Our protection is that all the houses are occupied and we are not likely to be asked to move them, but the uncertainty of tenure is such that the crown is hardly warranted in spending money on such houses. Before we sell a house to a veteran we put in a concrete foundation, if the house does not have one, and we replace the wartime steel chimney with a brick chimney, and generally put the house in first-class shape before we sell it to a private owner, who has rights to the property and security of tenure. That seems a better disposition of these houses than the present indefinite position.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
At page 3639 of Hansard the minister referred to encouragement given for the additional production of soil pipe and plumbing fixtures. Can he give us details of what assistance has been given? At page 3642 the minister refers to the discussions
National Housing Act

that have been held with the Canadian federation of mayors and intimated that there is a softening-up process and that, so far as he is concerned, he is prepared to discuss with the provinces and the municipalities solutions of present difficulties. When I raised the question in the house on March 18 as to whether the minister had given leadership in convening such a conference he replied, no. Can he state now whether there is any possibility of his taking the initiative in convening a conference with provincial and municipal authorities to discuss the whole question of housing?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
The minister meets with the provinces whenever they care to discuss with him any housing project, but he has had experience enough to know that representatives of nine provinces meeting in one room and holding diametrically opposite views can agree on nothing. If any province wishes to discuss any matter with me, and they practically all do from time to time, these discussions are held either in the province or in Ottawa.
There is nothing new to report on soil pipe or plumbing. Additional capacity was provided by Crane on a subsidy basis for excess production of bath fittings, on a basis of two cents a pound. The only other subsidy was to a firm in Winnipeg which had built additional capacity for producing soil pipe. I have not the details.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Earlier I asked a question in all seriousness in regard to the production of nails. Builders in Toronto are in a desperate position in regard to nails. Representations have been made to the minister's department to see what can be done to cut through whatever obstacles are holding up production. Apparently at the present time the wire is not available, and I understand that the minister has control of the disposition of wire materials to various firms. I wonder if he would make a statement, if not now, at any rate within the next day or so when he has all the facts before him. This is not a facetious matter; as far as I am concerned, it is of considerable importance.

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
I shall be glad to state the position. I thought everyone had understood it. The bottleneck is not in nail-making machinery, but in the amount of wire rod that this country is capable of producing. Wire rod is divided between nails, bailing wire, barbed wire fencing and one or two essential uses to which wire is put. We cannot step up the amount of wire which the rolling mills can produce. It would take years and a heavy capital investment to do so. All we can do is to divide as fairly as we can the material that

the mills can produce as between the manufacture of nails and the manufacture of other commodities. I have asked our people to give all the preference they dare to give to nails, and we are going to take a bite out of wire products. There will be complaints about that, but you cannot distribute more than there is in toto. We are in process of diverting wire from other uses into nails. We are not going to make any barbed wire for a few months. I hope hon. members who have been worrying about nails will not start worrying about other products, because that is the only way to get more nails. In March, 1948, we produced 142,000-odd kegs of nails as against 130,000 odd in March, 1947. We are producing more nails than we ever produced before, but the complaints continue. I am disposed to go full out and fill every hardware store with nails and have people complaining about something else for a while. That is what we are going to do. We shall doubtless get other complaints.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I do not think we should enter into any long discussion on nails on this resolution.

speakerposition: Whip of the Co-operative Commonwealth Federation
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: You cannot build houses without nails.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: We have to observe some order.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
There is one other feature to which I wish to refer. There are 12,000 wartime homes which the minister announced last October he was prepared to have built by Wartime Housing Limited, but apparently that number of houses will not be built because the municipalities have not all signified their intention of carrying on with the project. These projects have priority for nails, and the thought I am trying to express is that Wartime Housing Limited has been receiving more than its share of nails, and in respect of builders building under integrated housing, they have been receiving probably more from month to month than they should have been given. My informant, a reputable builder, tells me that when he went into a large wholesale house to get nails there was plenty available, but most of the nails went to three builders who were under the integrated plan, and the rest of the nails had to be divided among about 100 other builders. The hardware wholesaler was trying to do the best he could, but the fact was that the builder-I am referring to a private builder who incidentally carries on with the assistance and co-operation of Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation-could not get enough nails to go on with his project. Would the minister look into that to see whether or not some of these government agencies, such as Wartime Housing and integrated housing.

Royal Canadian Mounted Police Act
are getting more than the amount they need, to carry on from month to month, and whether others are getting their share?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: Any contractor who is building veterans' houses under any government plan can get his quota of nails. That quota is definite. His priority is for five kegs of nails per house, and that is all. I have looked into the stocks of nails in the hands of contractors for veterans houses, and they never exceed more than half a keg of nails per house under construction. It is all very well to theorize and to say that no one else can get nails because veterans houses get more than their share, but five kegs per house is, by all experience, the actual requirement for the type of house that is built under the government plan. The stock position is carefully watched. Everyone seems to feel that whereas he cannot get nails, everyone else has plenty. That is not the case at all. I do not know of anyone who has plenty. The veterans priority affords enough nails, which we guarantee under the government plan.

subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext: I have never spoken about nails before, but I am interested in nails today because I was approached on Saturday in my riding and told that nails were in scarce supply in Huntsville. I have a strong recollection that not long ago the minister said it was not a question of shortage but a question of distribution. Am I wrong in that?

speakerposition: Minister of Trade and Commerce; Minister of Reconstruction and Supply
subtopic: AMENDMENT WITH RESPECT TO POWERS OF APPROVED LENDING INSTITUTIONS, ETC.
speechtext:
Conditions change from
month to month. Speaking last winter, I said that the amount of nails produced was about equal to the amount consumed. This is the height of the building season, and builders are using more nails than they were when I made the statement about production being equal to consumption.
